Each cell draws exactly the item the scheme asks for (whole figure, or one panel of it) by reusing
`viz/frames.py` + `viz/plots.py`, and saves through `viz/save.py` into:

Notebooks 40–44 stay as they are (they are the computation and the check against the document);
46 is the "where does each graph go" layer. Numbers used in the document text come from the
`numbers.csv` of 40–44, never typed.

## Deliverable 2 — the document (`47_thesis_document.ipynb` + `viz/document.py` → markdown → docx + pdf)

Structure:
1. **Methodology** (one section, written once): the dataset in five lines; unit of analysis; windows; the
   tests used (one table: test, what it answers, formula); then per question Q1–Q8 one short paragraph
   (what is measured, on which base, with which figure). No results here.
2. **Results and discussion**: Q1…Q8 in the scheme's order and wording; per sub-question A/B/C/D the main-text
   figure(s)/table(s), two to four sentences of result, one of discussion. Answer box per question.
3. **Appendix**: per question, the appendix items of the table above, each with caption + one takeaway line.
4. Limitations (the "never tell you" section, cut to one page) — position to confirm.

Density rules: ≤ 2 figures per sub-question in the main text; captions ≤ 2 lines; no Source/Unit/How-to-read
triplets in the text (they stay in the figure json/csv for LaTeX); one number per sentence.
Voice: thesis-voice skill (impersonal, claims framed by what they establish).

## Methodology v2 — author's ruling 2026-10-07 (do AFTER the build + document run, as a second task)

The Methodology section is NOT prose. It is written so a reader understands the methods and the organisation of the
document first, with few words:
- **Topics, not paragraphs**: short labelled points (Objective · Data and unit · Procedure · Test · Limit), one line each,
  per question. No explanation beyond what is needed to follow; nothing said twice.
- **Flowcharts where they carry the understanding**: one chapter-level flowchart (ground files → 627 unique aircraft →
  the seven questions → their figures/tables → answers) and, per question, a small flow "data subset → transform →
  test → what the figure shows → answer". Draw them as figures the notebooks produce (matplotlib boxes-and-arrows via a
  small helper in viz/plots.py or TikZ in the .tex; the first is preferred so they are files in thesis_figures/<Q>/method/).
- **The statistics table stays** (test · what it answers · formula · used in); everything else about a test is one line.
- Also state in one place the organisation of the document (parts → questions → sub-questions → Answer box → appendix).
- Keep the conciseness rules of THESIS_CONTRACT.md §2; the goal is "understandable without a lot of words".
Implementation: change viz/thesis_text_common.py (METHOD_COMMON → topic list + CHAPTER_MAP + flowchart item) and each
viz/thesis_text_qN.py METHOD into a topic list (markup: lines starting with "- **Label:** text"), add `method` items
(slot "method", kind "figure") to viz/thesis.py SLOTS and each thesis_qN.py ITEMS, teach viz/thesis_doc.py to render
"- " lines as \begin{itemize} and to place the method flowchart under each question's Methodology subsection. Rebuild 46/47.
